rule: Fat-finger-labelled payments are disproportionately extreme in size versus comparable normal payments; an exact x10^k mechanism is not established
test: share of payments whose rounded log10 distance from the country x pair median is >= 2 (about 32x or more)
interpretation: Consistent with a keying slip that multiplies the amount by a power of 10

rule: Duplicates come in bursts of 2-5 identical payments (same sender, payee, currency and amount) about 18 minutes apart; every copy in these bursts is labelled, and an earlier unlabelled match is found no more often than by chance (no evidence of unlabelled originals)
test: burst structure of labelled duplicates; share with an earlier matching payment vs normal payments
value: 185 bursts of 2-5 copies, identical amount 100%, median 1099s apart; first copy with an earlier unlabelled match 9.2% (normal 9.2%); earlier match (any copy): 75.6% vs 9.4% control (diff +66.1% [+62.4%, +69.9%], p < 1e-300); 74.6% vs 8.3% control (diff +66.4% [+58.8%, +73.9%], p = 1.1e-87)
interpretation: Consistent with a back-office re-submission of the same instruction

rule: Business and consumer duplicates follow the same pattern: re-sent by the same sender, minutes later. The hypothesised consumer pattern (a different sender, hours or days later) is not found
test: same-sender share and gap to the matched original, by sender type (duplicates with a match)
interpretation: One re-submission pattern for both sender types; the B/C split in hypothesis A2 is not supported

rule: Romance scam: one consumer pays the same consumer several times within a day, with rising amounts
test: C2C pairs with 3+ payments: rising amounts and within-1-day share vs normal pairs
interpretation: Consistent with a victim being groomed into sending more and more

rule: CEO scam: business sender, first payment to a new payee, amount above the usual level
test: first-time payee share vs normal business payments; amount shift (Mann-Whitney)
interpretation: Consistent with a fake executive ordering an urgent transfer to a new supplier account

rule: Account-replacement scams: no earlier payment from the same sender to the same payee was found (exact party text, or first name line); the replacement mechanism is not recovered with these matching methods
test: earlier payment from the same sender (BIC8 + account) to the same payee: exact party text, then relaxed first-line name match (4.6b); the same exact-text match finds a predecessor for normal payments, so the method can find links
value: 0.0% vs 5.7% control (diff -5.7% [-6.4%, -5.1%], p = 3.7e-10); relaxed name match 0.2% [0.0%, 0.9%], n = 649, with a changed account 1
interpretation: The label is not tied to a payee history that these joins can see; names or details may be re-generated, so absence of a match does not prove absence of a link

rule: For labels outside the appendix (CUSTOMER_RECALL), no linked payment (same sender and receiver bank + account, amount +-1%) was found for almost all rows
test: share of these rows with no matching payment (observation only)
interpretation: Observation only: how recalls arise is unresolved (the label is not defined in the appendix; ask the organisers)

rule: Anomaly rates are not uniform: they differ by conversions, cross_border, hour_utc, pair, transaction_type, weekday_utc; no difference by qflag
test: chi-square per anomaly x segment (p < 0.001 counted)
value: 14 of 42 anomaly x segment tests significant: conversions, cross_border, hour_utc, pair, transaction_type, weekday_utc
interpretation: Each scam type concentrates in its own segments; the cause is not identified

rule: IBAN is used for every account of a bank country or for none; IBAN country = BIC country
test: countries with mixed formats; IBAN country match
value: 76 countries all-IBAN, 153 none, 0 mixed; country match 100.00%
interpretation: IBAN is a national standard, adopted country by country

rule: Non-IBAN account numbers that contain a currency code use the bank country's local currency
test: share of non-IBAN accounts with a 3-letter code; match
value: 13.3% contain a code; 99.6% of those = local currency
interpretation: Domestic account numbers often carry the account currency

rule: Each sender account number belongs to one bank and one party type; 2.4% of receiver account numbers recur under several banks, so every account history uses (BIC8, account)
test: share of account numbers with > 1 BIC / party type
interpretation: Account numbers are issued per bank, so the same number can exist at two banks

rule: Party details lines are at most 35 characters (SWIFT MT line format)
test: share of details texts with every line <= 35 characters
interpretation: The 4 x 35 character field of SWIFT MT messages

rule: Business parties get company-name tokens; consumers get person-name tokens
value: receiver B business 87.7%; receiver C person 90.8%
interpretation: Consistent with a name generator that depends on the party type

rule: Sender address country = sender bank country; the receiver's address country usually differs
test: share of address country = bank country
interpretation: Consistent with senders banking locally while receivers can live anywhere

rule: The numbered (1/2/3/ lines) and BIC-line formats never occur in the same details text; the other 80% match neither (free text: a residual class, not a tested third template)
test: share of details texts matching BOTH explicit formats (the rule predicts 0), both sides, full data
value: beneficiary: numbered 15.0%, BIC line 5.0%, neither (free text) 80.0%, both 0.000%; ordering: numbered 16.0%, BIC line 5.0%, neither (free text) 79.0%, both 0.000%
interpretation: Consistent with one format being chosen per party text; regex classes describe the text and do not show how the free text is generated

rule: No detectable difference in the trailing finance / stop-word line rate between any anomaly type and normal payments (gaps of up to about 3 points cannot be excluded)
test: difference in the share with a filler line, each anomaly type vs all normal payments (two-proportion z-test)
value: largest difference 3.3 points; 0 of 12 comparisons with p < 0.001, 1 with p < 0.05
interpretation: Consistent with filler text that carries no anomaly information; this does not show how the filler is generated or that it is random
